issues.description: Specification of get_param_as_list with delimiter is silent on conflict with auto_parse_qs_csv
issues.detail: The author has added a delimiter argument but has not stated, in the docstring proper, the precondition relating it to auto_parse_qs_csv. The test test_get_param_as_list_parse_qs_csv_vs_delimiter encodes a behavior — when csv pre-splitting has already produced a list, delimiter is silently ignored — that is nowhere stated as a postcondition in the API contract. A user reading the docstring will not learn this. The Note hints at it obliquely ("if the parameter was already passed as an array") but does not mention auto_parse_qs_csv as a path to that array state. Either state the postcondition explicitly or refuse the silent ignore.

issues.description: Delimiter validation is a leaky abstraction: the key set conflates characters and symbolic names
issues.detail: _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS maps both literal characters (',', '|', ' ') and OpenAPI symbolic constants ('pipeDelimited', 'spaceDelimited') into a single namespace. There is no invariant stated that the symbolic constants and their character equivalents must agree, nor any test pinning that invariant. A future contributor who adds, say, 'tabDelimited' -> '\t' but forgets to also add '\t' as a key (or vice versa) breaks symmetry silently. Split the two concerns: one set of accepted literal delimiters, one map from symbolic name to literal. The current structure cannot be reasoned about as a single mathematical object.

issues.description: Error message leaks an implementation-order detail (dict insertion order) into the public contract
issues.detail: The ValueError reports `tuple(_PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS)` — a tuple whose order is the dict's insertion order. This is observable, untested, and unspecified. It is exactly the kind of incidental property that becomes load-bearing the moment someone writes a test against the message text. Sort the keys, or partition them into characters and symbolic names with a stable presentation. Do not let implementation order escape into messages users will read and possibly assert against.

issues.description: No test for empty-string or single-token splitting behavior
issues.detail: The postcondition for items.split(delim) on inputs like '', 'Luke', or 'Luke,' is not pinned by any test. Python's str.split returns [''], ['Luke'], and ['Luke', ''] respectively. The interaction with keep_blank_qs_values is mentioned in the docstring as having no effect on the secondary split, but no test demonstrates the behavior on blanks. The reader cannot determine, from the tests, whether 'names=' followed by delimiter='|' yields [''] or [] or raises. State the postcondition and pin it.

issues.description: Termination and frame trivial but unstated; control flow is mercifully structured
issues.detail: The added block is a straight selection followed by an assignment — no smuggled goto, no flag, no early return. Termination is trivial (str.split is finite). I note this only because the rest of get_param_as_list has accreted enough conditional branching that a future addition of 'just one more case' would push the function past the threshold where a reader can hold the control flow in their head. The competent programmer is fully aware of the limited size of his own skull; this function is approaching that limit and should be watched.

issues.description: Type annotation `delimiter: str | None = None` admits values that the runtime then refuses
issues.detail: The type says str. The runtime accepts five specific strings and raises on all others. This is TESTED-NOT-PROVED rather than refused outright, but the type system is being used as decoration rather than specification. A Literal type listing the five accepted values would let mypy reject the bad-delimiter call site at static-check time rather than at runtime. This is exactly the discipline of stating the precondition in a form the machine can verify.

review.summary: The patch is small, structured, and — by the low standards of modern feature-addition PRs — not actively offensive. The added control flow is a selection followed by an assignment; there is no smuggled goto. However, the author has not stated the precondition in a form the type system can verify (delimiter is typed as str but only five strings are accepted), the interaction with auto_parse_qs_csv is encoded in a test rather than asserted as a postcondition in the docstring, and the _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS table conflates literal delimiters with symbolic OpenAPI names in a single namespace with no invariant tying the two halves together. The error message leaks dict insertion order into a user-visible string. Verdict: REASONED but with TESTED-NOT-PROVED scaffolding around the boundary cases. Acceptable with the P1 items addressed; the P2 items are the discipline the next maintainer will wish had been observed.
